transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because something’s been happening at work that really scared me. During quiet times in the surveillance room, I hear voices coming through the monitor speakers, saying things like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or that people are going to get hurt because of me. But all the channels are muted, and nobody else hears them.
How long ago did you first start hearing these voices, and have they been happening continuously since then?

It started during those quiet stretches in the surveillance room. I hear the voices through the speakers even though everything is muted, and nobody else can hear them. They say things like I missed something, or that people will get hurt because of me.
Since these voices first started, how many days or weeks in total have you been experiencing them?
It’s been about four months now, since I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role.

Besides these voices, have you noticed any other unusual experiences—like difficulty organizing your thoughts, trouble keeping up with daily tasks, becoming more withdrawn, or believing things that others don't believe, like feeling watched or targeted?

I keep going over every missed camera angle or call I was slow to make. It feels like proof that I’m careless, that I could be dangerous to people. And... if something does go wrong, part of me thinks I deserve to be punished for it.
Over these past four months, have you been feeling persistently down, hopeless, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah. Most days there’s this heavy gray feeling over me before I even get out of bed. I’ve found myself tearing up in my car before a shift over something as small as seeing the casino lights.
Do you hear these voices only during times when you're feeling that heavy, down mood, or do they also happen when your mood feels more normal?

Only when I’m in this low stretch. Before I started feeling so hopeless and guilty after the lead change, I’d never heard anything like that or felt so sure I was dangerous to people. They seem to go together.

latest_inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (mood-congruent guilt-themed auditory hallucinations, delusional guilt) occur exclusively during the depressive episode and remit outside it, per patient report. This rules out F20.9 (schizophrenia, which requires psychosis independent of mood) and F25.1 (schizoaffective disorder, which requires psychotic symptoms present without mood symptoms for a significant period). F28 is no longer needed since the presentation fits classic mood-congruent psychotic depression rather than an atypical psychotic disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a single episode of at least 4 months duration characterized by persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, guilt, hopelessness, and psychomotor/emotional heaviness, accompanied by mood-congruent psychotic features—auditory hallucinations (voices blaming her for harm) and delusions of guilt/responsibility (belief she deserves punishment). Critically, the patient confirms these psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the depressive episodes and were absent before the mood disturbance began, indicating the psychosis is secondary to and congruent with the depressive episode rather than a primary psychotic or schizoaffective disorder. This pattern is most consistent with Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe with Psychotic Features (F32.3), rather than schizophrenia (F20.9) or schizoaffective disorder (F25.1), which would require psychotic symptoms independent of mood episodes.
